sentences.zh: 一：東京遼陽府至號中京顯德府「本朝鮮之地」，據史記一一五朝鮮傳、漢書二八下地理志，應作「本燕國地」。

translations.literal: 1 From Eastern Capital Liaoyang Prefecture through styled Central Capital Xiande Prefecture: "originally Chaoxian territory"—according to Shiji 115 Chaoxian Traditions and Hanshu 28b Geographic Treatise, it should read "originally Yan state territory."
translations.idiomatic: First note: from Eastern Capital Liaoyang Prefecture through "Central Capital Xiande Prefecture," the phrase "originally Chaoxian territory" should, per Shiji 115 and Hanshu 28b, read "originally Yan state territory."

translations.literal: This section wrongly takes Liaoyang for Pyongyang.
translations.idiomatic: This section wrongly identifies Liaoyang with Pyongyang.

sentences.zh: 又據新唐書二一九渤海傳，忽汗州爲上京龍泉府，非平壤城，亦非遼陽。

translations.literal: Moreover, according to New Tang History 219 Bohai Traditions, Hohan Prefecture was Shangjing Longquan Prefecture—not Pyongyang, and not Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Per New Tang History 219 Bohai Traditions, Hohan Prefecture was Shangjing Longquan Prefecture, not Pyongyang or Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 二：太祖建國攻渤海撥忽汗城至神冊四年葺遼陽故城建東平郡爲防禦州按葺遼陽故城、建東平郡在前，攻渤海、撥忽汗城在後，敘次倒舛。

translations.literal: 2 From Taizu founding the state and attacking Bohai through seizing Hohan city to Shence year 4 repairing Liaoyang old walls and building Dongping Commandery as defense prefecture: repairing Liaoyang and building Dongping come first; attacking Bohai and seizing Hohan come after—the narrative order is inverted.
translations.idiomatic: Second note: repairing Liaoyang and founding Dongping precede the Bohai campaign and seizure of Hohan—the sequence is inverted.

sentences.zh: 疑神冊四年之前脫「先是」二字。

translations.literal: It is suspected that "formerly" two characters were lost before Shence year 4.
translations.idiomatic: Likely "formerly" was lost before Shence year 4.

sentences.zh: 三：城名天福按紀天顯元年二月，改忽汗城爲天福。

translations.literal: 3 City named Tianfu: according to the Annals, Tianxian year 1 second month changed Hohan city to Tianfu.
translations.idiomatic: Third note: "city named Tianfu"—the Annals place the Hohan-to-Tianfu rename in Tianxian year 1, month 2.

sentences.zh: 非升東平爲南京時以東平爲天福。

translations.literal: It was not when Dongping was raised to Nanjing that Dongping was called Tianfu.
translations.idiomatic: Tianfu was not the name given when Dongping became Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 四：轄州府軍城八十七按「八十七」與下文所列州、府、軍、城之數不合。

translations.literal: 4 Governing eighty-seven prefectures, fu, armies, and cities: the figure "eighty-seven" does not match the list of prefectures, fu, armies, and cities below.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth note: "eighty-seven" prefectures, fu, armies, and cities does not match the list below.

sentences.zh: 五：本漢鏤芳縣地鏤芳，漢書地理志、後漢書郡國志均作鏤方，屬樂浪郡。

translations.literal: 5 "Originally Han Loufang County land": Loufang—in Hanshu Geographic Treatise and Hou Hanshu Commanderies and States both write Loufang, belonging to Lelang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth note: "Loufang County"—Hanshu and Hou Hanshu both have Loufang in Lelang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 六：聖宗伐高麗還高麗原誤「新羅」，據紀統和三年七月、十年正月改。

translations.literal: 6 "Shengzong returned from campaigning Goryeo": the original erroneously read "Silla"; corrected per Annals Tonghe year 3 seventh month and year 10 first month.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth note: "Goryeo" was written "Silla" in the original; corrected from Annals Tonghe 3.7 and 10.1.

sentences.zh: 七：統和末高麗降「統和末，高麗降」六字，原誤在「開泰三年，取其保、定二州」之下，時間倒舛，今改。

translations.literal: 7 "At the end of Tonghe Goryeo surrendered"—the six characters "at the end of Tonghe, Goryeo surrendered" were wrongly placed after "Kaitai year 3 took its Bao and Ding two prefectures," reversing chronology; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh note: "at Tonghe's end Goryeo surrendered" was misplaced after the Kaitai seizure of Bao and Ding—now reordered.

sentences.zh: 八：河端道光殿本考證引永樂大典作河瑞。

translations.literal: 8 Heduan: Daoguang Hall edition Commentary cites Yongle Encyclopedia as Herui.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth note: Heduan—Daoguang Commentary cites Yongle Encyclopedia's Herui.

sentences.zh: 九：渤海置州「渤海置州」四字原脫，道光殿本據通考增。

translations.literal: 9 "Bohai established the prefecture"—the four characters "Bohai established the prefecture" were originally missing; Daoguang Hall edition added them per Tongkao.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth note: "Bohai established the prefecture" was missing; Daoguang edition restored it from Tongkao.

translations.literal: The present text follows that.
translations.idiomatic: The present text follows that addition.

sentences.zh: 一○：淇水按趙萬里輯元一統志

translations.literal: 10 Qi River: according to Zhao Wanli's collated Yuan Comprehensive Gazetteer
translations.idiomatic: Tenth note: Qi River—per Zhao Wanli's collated Yuan Comprehensive Gazetteer

translations.literal: Opening angle bracket in the citation title.
translations.idiomatic: Opening bracket before the abbreviated gazetteer title.

translations.literal: (hereafter called Collated Yuan Comprehensive Gazetteer); closing bracket.
translations.idiomatic: The text continues as the Collated Yuan Comprehensive Gazetteer, then closes the citation bracket.

translations.literal: Volume 2 has Water.
translations.idiomatic: Volume 2 lists Water.

translations.literal: The character "Qi" is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The character Qi is erroneous.

sentences.zh: 一一：本漢東耐縣地道光殿本考證謂，漢無東耐縣，或是後漢書郡國志東、不而之脫誤。

translations.literal: 11 "Originally Han Dongnai County land": Daoguang Hall edition Commentary says Han had no Dongnai County; it may be a dropped-graph error for Hou Hanshu Commanderies and States' "Dong" and "Buer."
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh note: Dongnai County—Daoguang Commentary argues Han lacked Dongnai; likely a garble of Hou Hanshu's Dong and Buer counties.

sentences.zh: 索隱疑是唐羈縻代那州。

translations.literal: Suoyin suspects it is Tang's tributary Daina Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Suoyin suggests Tang's tributary Daina Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 一二：率賓縣本渤海率賓府地索隱：「既云遷率賓府人戶置，則非故地。」

translations.literal: 12 Suibin County "originally Bohai Suibin Prefecture land": Suoyin: "Since it says Suibin Prefecture households were moved to establish it, it is not the old territory."
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth note: Suoyin observes that relocating Suibin Prefecture households means it is not the original territory.

sentences.zh: 一三：乾州聖宗統和三年置按紀乾亨四年十一月置乾州。

translations.literal: 13 Qian Prefecture "Shengzong Tonghe year 3 established": according to the Annals, Qianzhou was established in Qianheng year 4 eleventh month.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteenth note: Qian Prefecture's Tonghe year 3—Annals place it in Qianheng year 4, month 11.

translations.literal: 14 Xuan Prefecture: "Xuan" should be Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteenth note: Xuan should read Yi.

translations.literal: This is Zhongjing Circuit's Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: This is Yi Prefecture of Zhongjing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 屬縣開義，金史地理志同，本書中京道宜州條下作聞義。

translations.literal: Its county Kaiyi matches Jin History Geographic Treatise; this book's Zhongjing Circuit Yi Prefecture entry writes Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate Kaiyi County matches Jin History; this book's Zhongjing Yi entry reads Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 一五：漢公孫度所據依上下文例，漢下脫「末」字。

translations.literal: 15 "Han Gongsun Du held it"—by context "late" is missing after Han.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteenth note: "Han Gongsun Du held it"—context requires "late Han."

sentences.zh: 一六：本渤海緣城縣地緣城，上文崇州條作綠城。

translations.literal: 16 "Originally Bohai Yuancheng County land": Yuancheng—in the Chong Prefecture entry above appears as Lücheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteenth note: Yuancheng appears as Lücheng in the Chong Prefecture entry above.

sentences.zh: 一七：渤海建瀋州故縣九皆廢道光殿本考證：「按元一統志，渤海建定理府，都督瀋、定二州，領定理、平邱、岩城、慕美、安夷、瀋水、安定、保山、能利九縣，並廢。」

translations.literal: 17 "Bohai built Shen Prefecture; nine former counties all abolished"—Daoguang Hall edition Commentary: "According to the Yuan Comprehensive Gazetteer, Bohai built Dingli Prefecture, superintending Shen and Ding two prefectures, governing Dingli, Pingqiu, Yancheng, Meimei, Anyi, Shenshui, Anding, Baoshan, and Nengli nine counties—all abolished."
translations.idiomatic: Seventeenth note: Daoguang Commentary cites Yuan Comprehensive Gazetteer—Bohai's Dingli Prefecture oversaw nine counties, all abolished.

sentences.zh: 一八：初隸永興宮宮字原脫，據營衛志上補。

translations.literal: 18 "At first subordinate to Yongxing Palace"—the character "palace" was originally missing, restored from Barracks and Guards Treatise, upper.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteenth note: "Yongxing Palace" lacked palace, restored from Barracks and Guards Treatise, upper.

sentences.zh: 一九：伊蒙陀黑北五州北，新唐書二一九渤海傳作比。

translations.literal: 19 "Yi, Meng, Tuo, Hei, Bei five prefectures": Bei—in New Tang History 219 Bohai Traditions appears as Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteenth note: Bei prefecture appears as Bi in New Tang History 219.

sentences.zh: 二○：祺州祺，原誤「棋」，據營衛志上及金史地理志改。

translations.literal: 20 Qi Prefecture: Qi was originally written "chess" Qi; corrected per Barracks and Guards Treatise, upper, and Jin History Geographic Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Twentieth note: Qi was written with the "chess" graph; corrected from Barracks and Guards and Jin History.

sentences.zh: 二一：聖宗更今名至升節度按聖宗在景宗保寧之後。

translations.literal: 21 "Shengzong changed to the present name through raising to military commissioner": Shengzong came after Jingzong's Baoning.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-first note: Shengzong's rename followed Jingzong's Baoning era.

sentences.zh: 景宗保寧七年已增置戶口，升節度，聖宗時，始更名通州。

translations.literal: Jingzong Baoning year 7 had already added households and raised it to military commissioner; only under Shengzong was it renamed Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Baoning year 7 already added households and a military commission; Shengzong then renamed it Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二二：強帥縣金史地理志作強師縣。

translations.literal: 22 Qiangshuai County: Jin History Geographic Treatise writes Qiangshi County.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-second note: Qiangshuai County is Qiangshi in Jin History.

sentences.zh: 二三：頡府都督頡二州按新唐書二一九渤海傳，頡府領、高二州。

translations.literal: 23 "Xie Prefecture superintending Xie two prefectures": according to New Tang History 219 Bohai Traditions, Xie Prefecture governed Xie and Gao two prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-third note: Bohai's Xie Prefecture governed Xie and Gao, per New Tang History 219.

sentences.zh: 二四：郝里太保城郝，紀開泰八年十月作耗。

translations.literal: 24 Haoli Grand Guardian Fort: Hao—in the Annals Kaitai year 8 tenth month appears as Hao (waste).
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-fourth note: Haoli appears as Hao in Annals Kaitai 8.10.

sentences.zh: 二五：信州彰聖軍下節度按百官志四作信州彰聖軍節度，同。

translations.literal: 25 Xin Prefecture "Zhangsheng Army lower military commissioner": according to Officials Treatise 4 it is Xin Prefecture Zhangsheng Army military commissioner—the same.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-fifth note: Officials Treatise 4 agrees on Xin Prefecture Zhangsheng Army military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 卷九一耶律僕里篤傳，太平中累遷彰聖軍節度使，紀大安八年有彰聖軍節度使耶律涅里。

translations.literal: Juan 91 Yelü Pulidu Traditions—in Taiping times he was repeatedly promoted to Zhangsheng Army military commissioner; Annals Da'an year 8 has Zhangsheng Army military commissioner Yelü Nieli.
translations.idiomatic: Juan 91 Yelü Pulidu rose to Zhangsheng Army commissioner in Taiping; Da'an year 8 names Yelü Nieli.

sentences.zh: 下文郢州，軍號與信州同，但爲刺史州，非節鎮。

translations.literal: Below, Ying Prefecture shares the army title with Xin Prefecture but is a cishi prefecture, not a circuit command.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Prefecture shares Xin's army title but is a cishi prefecture, not a circuit seat.

sentences.zh: 百官志四刺史州內有郢州。

translations.literal: Officials Treatise 4 lists Ying Prefecture among cishi prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Officials Treatise 4 classifies Ying among cishi prefectures.

sentences.zh: 又皇子表及卷八二蕭陽阿傳有彰信軍節度，金史地理志作信州彰信軍。

translations.literal: Moreover, Princes Table and Juan 82 Xiao Yang'a Traditions have Zhangxin Army military commissioner; Jin History Geographic Treatise writes Xin Prefecture Zhangxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: Princes Table and Xiao Yang'a also mention Zhangxin Army; Jin History has Zhangxin at Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二六：置刺史于鴨子混同二水之間按紀太平四年二月，「詔改鴨子河曰混同江」，但此後仍沿用鴨子河名稱，卷九八耶律儼傳：「父仲禧┅┅清寧四年城鴨子、混同二水間。」

translations.literal: 26 "Placed cishi between Yazi and Hunton two rivers":—according to the Annals Taiping year 4 second month: "An edict changed Yazi River to Hunton River," but afterward the name Yazi River was still used; Juan 98 Yelü Yan Traditions: "His father Zhongxi—Qingning year 4 walled between Yazi and Hunton two waters."
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-sixth note: Annals Taiping 4.2 renamed Yazi River Hunton River, yet Yazi River remained in use; Yelü Yan records Zhongxi walling between the two waters in Qingning 4.

sentences.zh: 二七：黃龍府都部署司司，原誤「事」。

translations.literal: 27 "Huanglong Prefecture Deployment Office": Office—the original erroneously read "affairs"; corrected per context, Military Treatise middle, Barracks and Guards lower, and Officials Treatise 2.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-seventh note: "Deployment Office" was written "affairs"; corrected from context and parallel treatises.

sentences.zh: 據上下文及兵衛志中、營衛志下、百官志二改。

translations.literal: According to context and Military Treatise middle, Barracks and Guards lower, and Officials Treatise 2 corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected from Military Treatise, Barracks and Guards, and Officials Treatise 2.

sentences.zh: 二八：安定府按紀天顯元年三月作安邊府。

translations.literal: 28 Anding Prefecture: according to the Annals Tianxian year 1 third month it was Anbian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-eighth note: Anding Prefecture was Anbian in Annals Tianxian 1.3.

sentences.zh: 二九：復州懷德軍節度按金史地理志：「復州，下，刺史，遼懷遠軍節度。」

translations.literal: 29 Fu Prefecture Huaide Army military commissioner: according to Jin History Geographic Treatise: "Fu Prefecture, lower, cishi; Liao Huaiyuan Army military commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-ninth note: Jin History lists Fu as cishi with Liao Huaiyuan Army military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三○：安州刺史按紀統和二十八年十一月，馬保佑曾爲安州團練使，卷九四耶律何魯掃古傳，清寧初加安州團練使，百官志四亦作團練。

translations.literal: 30 An Prefecture cishi: according to the Annals Tonghe year 28 eleventh month, Ma Baoyou once was An Prefecture regional training commissioner; Juan 94 Yelü Helu Saogu Traditions, early Qingning added An Prefecture regional training commissioner; Officials Treatise 4 also writes regional training.
translations.idiomatic: Thirtieth note: Annals Tonghe 28.11 names Ma Baoyou An regional training commissioner; Yelü Helu Saogu and Officials Treatise 4 agree.

sentences.zh: 惟國志二二刺史州內有安州。

translations.literal: Only State Chronicles 22 lists An among cishi prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Only State Chronicles 22 lists An as a cishi prefecture.

translations.literal: Perhaps at first it was cishi and later raised to regional training.
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps it began as cishi and was later raised to regional training.

sentences.zh: 卷一 ○五蕭文傳，「父直善，安州防禦使。

translations.literal: Juan 105 Xiao Wen Traditions: "Father Zhishan, An Prefecture defense commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: Juan 105 Xiao Wen Traditions: "Father Zhishan was An Prefecture defense commissioner."

translations.literal: Civil office in the Dakang and Shouchang period.
translations.idiomatic: He held civil office during Dakang and Shouchang.
